plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. This means there's no incentive to overbid or underbid—truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. My value is $2, so I will bid exactly $2 to ensure I only win when profitable (i.e., when the second-highest bid is below my value) and avoid overpaying.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what others do. Since my value is $33, bidding exactly $33 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids and never overpay, while losing when I shouldn't. There's no benefit to shading since payment is based on the second-highest bid, not my own bid.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a loss, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $43, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my valuation, ensuring I maximize expected profit without altering the incentive structure of the auction.
